title: DCDIR: A Deep Cross-Domain Recommendation System for Cold Start Users in Insurance Domain
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: DCDIR transfers e-commerce preferences to cold-start insurance users using knowledge-graph meta-paths, GRUs and an MLP mapping.
rq2_evaluation: Train/Validation/Test split. Metrics: Recall@3, NDCG.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Meta-path based method over KG; paper states it "reveals reasons behind recommendations" and can provide "interpretable recommendations". Transparency: Moderate (Meta-paths offer some insight, but GRU/MLP parts are black-box).
contribution: DCDIR transfers e-commerce preferences to cold-start insurance users using knowledge-graph meta-paths, GRUs and an MLP mapping.
data_description: User implicit interaction sequences (insurance & non-financial domains), Insurance product knowledge graph (ISKG) with entities (Product, Feature, Need) and relations, Item descriptions (source domain).
data_source: Internal company dataset (PingAn Jinguanjia - PAJGJ); Constructed ISKG. Sub-dataset named JGJISNF released.
data_size: JGJISNF: 42 IS items, 3836 NF items, ~300k IS interactions, ~600k NF interactions, 21,016 overlapping users. ISKG: 7 relations, 77 entities, 282 triples. Original dataset ~20M users.
time_characteristics: Uses chronological user behavior sequences. Data collected June 2018 - May 2019. GRU models temporal sequence. Meta-path scoring considers recency.
preprocessing: Word2vec for source item descriptions. TransD pre-training for KG embeddings. Meta-path generation & scoring. Construction of user sequences.
method_details: TransD embeddings and meta-path scoring represent insurance knowledge; a GRU aggregates paths. A second GRU models source-domain sequences. An MLP maps source to target user features; dot-product or DNN scoring ranks items.
architecture: Two-branch network (source/target feature extraction) + MLP mapping function. Target branch: KG embedding (TransD) -> Meta-path sampling/scoring -> GRU aggregation. Source branch: Item embedding (Word2Vec) -> GRU.
training: Joint optimization of recommendation loss (BPR-like with negative sampling) in both domains and mapping loss (MSE between mapped source features and target features for overlapping users). Adam optimizer. KG pre-training.
metrics: Recall@3, NDCG
baselines: BPR, GRU4Rec, EMCDR-BPR, EMCDR-GRU). Also compares against DCDIR variants (DCDIR-V1: attributes+KGE, DCDIR-V2: KGE 2-hop aggregation
evaluation_protocol: Train/Validation/Test split. Test set = 30% overlapping users treated as cold-start in target domain. Negative sampling (1 neg per pos). Evaluation across different overlap ratios (η=10%, 20%, 50%, 100%).
temporal_method: GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) on user interaction sequences (source domain). Meta-path scoring function incorporates interaction time/recency (target domain).
temporal_aspects: User dynamic interests based on sequence order (source domain). Recency bias in interaction importance (target domain, via meta-path scoring).
explanation_method: Meta-path based method over KG; paper states it "reveals reasons behind recommendations" and can provide "interpretable recommendations".
transparency: Moderate (Meta-paths offer some insight, but GRU/MLP parts are black-box).
implementation: TransD, GRU, MLP and meta-path components described. Embedding size 50; dropout 0.8; learning rate 0.001; batch size 32; 20 paths; top-k path generation; Word2vec.
open_science: JGJISNF dataset release reported; code release not reported.

financial_domain: Insurance Service / Business Intelligence (BI) in Insurance
contribution: RU-GOLAM combines GraphOLAM aggregation with node similarity to recommend insurance products using graph topology and user attributes.
data_description: Insurance sales transaction data (non-motor vehicle). User personal info (gender, constellation, age level, zodiac, car own.) used for aggregation. Social network constructed based on co-occurrence in insurance docs (policyholder, insured, beneficiary).
data_source: Private dataset from a "well-known insurance company in China".
data_size: Constructed social network: 222k nodes, 235k edges. Largest connected component used: 201k nodes, 212k edges. 658 insurance types. Aggregated graphs: e.g., 1518 nodes/140k edges (personal attrs), 1044 nodes/21k edges (behavioral attrs).
time_characteristics: Time not used in model
preprocessing: Constructing a social network graph from co-occurrence. Extracting largest connected component. Using 21 user attributes for dimension aggregation. Defining specific attribute aggregation hierarchies (e.g., personal vs behavioral).
method_details: GraphOLAM roll-up creates hierarchical graph views from user attributes. Similarities combine topology and attributes within and across levels. RA, cosine and dot-product measures are examined; UPP-SNE with dot product is used in the main experiment.
architecture: 3-layer: UI, RU-GOLAM engine, Backend DB (HDFS, HBase, Alluxio cache). Uses P&D Graph Cube model for storage. Core engine has Cube Engine (for roll-up) and RS Algorithm components (similarity calc). Generates multiple aggregated graph layers.
training: Network embedding (UPP-SNE) is trained. Node similarity is calculated based on embeddings & graph structure (original + aggregated). OLAP cube operations (roll-up) are performed. No explicit recommendation ranking training beyond similarity calculation.
metrics: Precision, Recall, F1-score @ K (K=3, 5, 10)
baselines: CF, DeepWalk, Node2Vec, GraphSage, RA Similarity [baseline], UPP-SNE [baseline]

temporal_method: Not reported.
temporal_aspects: Not reported.
explanation_method: Not reported.
transparency: Low

contribution: GubaLex sentiment analysis and a probabilistic neural network filter and rank Chinese stocks using bullishness, sentiment effectiveness and bear-market warnings.

data_source: Guba (online financial social media platforms: Sina Guba, Eastmoney Guba), RESSET financial database.

PNN training for efficiency classification.

architecture: Conceptual (Fig 1: Guba -> Corpus -> GubaLex -> Sentiment Measurement -> Ranking/Classification -> Recommendation). Uses PNN for classification step.

metrics: Correlation coefficient, Granger causality test, PNN Accuracy, Backtesting cumulative profit/net value.
baselines: CSI300 index (benchmark for backtesting).

transparency: Moderate (Rules are explicit, sentiment calculation logic is described, but PNN classification is black-box, lexicon construction has manual/complex parts).
implementation: Jieba segmentation; GubaLex construction and updating; sentiment weights and Bt/PVt/At formulas; PNN classifier and backtest strategy described.

title: Stock Recommendations for Individual Investors: A Temporal Graph Network Approach with Mean-Variance Efficient Sampling
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: PfoTGNRec combines temporal graph embeddings with mean-variance-efficient sampling and portfolio-aware ranking for personalized stock recommendations; code and data release are reported.
rq2_evaluation: Chronological split (80% train, 10% valid, 10% test). Metrics: Recommendation: HR@k, NDCG@k (k=3, 5). Investment: Return, Sharpe Ratio, P(SR)@k, P(R)@k (k=3, 5) (Improvement % for users), ΔSR, ΔR (Avg improvement). Combined metric: Weighted average m@5(α).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Explanation method not reported. Transparency: Low (Deep learning model, TGN, Attention are complex).
contribution: PfoTGNRec combines temporal graph embeddings with mean-variance-efficient sampling and portfolio-aware ranking for personalized stock recommendations; code and data release are reported.
data_description: User-stock interactions (buy orders), user portfolios (constructed from buy/sell orders), daily adjusted closing stock prices (used as edge features).
data_source: National Bank of Greece investor transaction dataset [29], Yahoo Finance (yfinance Python package) for stock prices.
data_size: 8,337 users, 92 stocks, 152,084 interactions after filtering. Data from Jan 2018 - Nov 2022. Avg interactions/user=18.24, avg stocks/portfolio=6.26.
time_characteristics: Data spans ~5 years. Uses continuous-time dynamic graph representation. Models temporal dynamics of preferences and stock features. Temporal edge features (30 days closing prices). Out-of-sample investment evaluation over next 30 days.
preprocessing: Filtering stocks (based on price stability, availability in yfinance). Constructing user portfolios over time. Retrieving daily adjusted closing prices as temporal edge features. methods: hybrid, collaborative, other (temporal graph network, deep learning)
method_details: A TGN encoder [28] uses GRU memory [3] and graph attention [28, 41]. MVEC sampling [4] forms contrastive pairs using expected return and variance over the next 30 days. BPR loss [27] trains the model; final ranks combine preference and portfolio criteria.
architecture: PfoTGNRec (Fig 2): Dynamic Embedding Learning (TGN: Memory + Graph Embedding using Attention) + Mean-Variance Efficient Sampling + BPR Optimization.
training: Train TGN encoder using BPR loss on positive/negative pairs sampled via Mean-Variance Efficient sampling strategy. The sampling ranks candidate items based on a weighted combination of preference (user interaction) and portfolio efficiency (mean-variance score). Selects top item as positive, bottom items as negative. 20 epochs training. Model selection based on validation set performance (avg rank of NDCG@5 and P(SR)@5). Hyperparameter tuning conducted.
metrics: Recommendation: HR@k, NDCG@k (k=3, 5). Investment: Return, Sharpe Ratio, P(SR)@k, P(R)@k (k=3, 5) (Improvement % for users), ΔSR, ΔR (Avg improvement). Combined metric: Weighted average m@5(α).
baselines: Static CF: Pop, WMF, BPR, LightGCN, SGL. Dynamic Graph: DyRep, Jodie, TGAT, TGN. Price-based: Return, Sharpe. Stock Rec.: two-step [31], MVECF [4].
evaluation_protocol: Chronological split (80% train, 10% valid, 10% test). Interaction-based ranking evaluation. Investment performance evaluated out-of-sample (next 30 days return/volatility). Recommended portfolio created by adding top K recommended stocks to original portfolio. Compared original vs recommended portfolio performance. Hyperparameter study conducted (batch size, node dim, candidate #, negative #, γ, λmv).
temporal_method: Temporal Graph Network (TGN) encoder, GRU for memory update, dynamic graph representation (continuous time), temporal edge features (past 30-day prices), interaction timestamps.
temporal_aspects: Captures evolving user preferences and stock characteristics through dynamic embeddings. Models interaction timing explicitly. Considers temporal neighbors. Uses recent price history as edge features. Analyzes investment performance over a future time window.
explanation_method: Not reported.
transparency: Low (Deep learning model, TGN, Attention are complex).
implementation: Architecture (Fig. 2); memory, graph, mean-variance, BPR and combined-ranking formulas; hyperparameter study (Fig. 4); data source and filtering described.

metrics: Reach Rate (RR), Clickthrough Rate (CTR), Purchase Rate (PR) for online A/B test. Precision, Recall for offline tests. Gross purchase value comparison.
baselines: Compared against 'conventional strategies (CS)' in use at the bank for the online A/B test. Compared against WAU baseline for offline Precision/Recall
evaluation_protocol: Online A/B test on a money market fund (TK) comparing BTUDE vs. CS over 5 days. Offline evaluation using Precision/Recall on target lists for a wealth management product (BSX) and life insurance (SBW) over 1 month (Sept 2022), comparing BTUDE list performance against assuming all WAU purchased. GMM fitting results shown graphically.
temporal_method: VAE with ResNet1D processes 52-week time series behavioural data. KDE normalization is applied to the time series.
temporal_aspects: Customer behavioral patterns over a 52-week period. Captures dynamic changes in user activity (logins, transactions, assets).
explanation_method: Unsupervised embedding (BTUDE) represents customer behaviour pattern; Similarity to known buyers and GMM clustering provides the rationale for recommendation, but VAE/ResNet are black-box.
transparency: Low (VAE/ResNet are black-box).
implementation: ResNet1D layers (Table I), KDE normalization and VAE loss (Eqs. 4–6) specified. A 2-component GMM uses cosine scores against the average profile of 320 random buyers; Spark-cluster evaluation.

rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Mentions analyzing the user embedding space as a direction for explainability. Transparency: Low (Transformer model is largely a black-box).
contribution: BRec uses self-attention over monthly customer metadata and product ownership for banking-product recommendation, with Santander ranking and beyond-accuracy evaluation.

data_source: Public Kaggle dataset: "Santander Product Recommendation".

time_characteristics: Explicitly models monthly sequences (17 months total, 16 for training, predict 17th). Uses temporal context heavily. Input representation encodes year, month, metadata, and product ownership at each time step.
preprocessing: Normalization of numerical metadata [0,1]. One-hot encoding for categorical metadata (Segment) and month. Binary encoding for year. Handling missing values (replace with Null category or sample mean). Creation of fixed-length sequences (16 months) with specific encoding structure (Fig 2). Masking items already owned in the final prediction period.
method_details: A BERT-like multi-head self-attention encoder represents monthly metadata and owned products as letters within words. A feed-forward layer and softmax predict the next acquisition; owned items are masked.
architecture: Transformer Encoder (6 layers, 7 heads, hidden size 2048) -> Feed Forward Layer -> Softmax. Includes batch normalization and dropout (0.5).
training: Supervised learning. Binary cross-entropy loss. Adam optimizer with RAdam warm-up schedule (peak 5 epochs, decay till 20). Training in batches (size 32).
metrics: Prec@k, Rec@k (k=1, 5, 10), MRR, NDCG. Also analyzes Serendipity@k, Novelty@k, Coverage@k (k=1, 5).
baselines: SASRec, TiSASRec, BERT4Rec, MEANTIME

temporal_aspects: User's product ownership history over time, user's metadata changes over time (age, income, seniority, segment), sequence order effects, relative time intervals implicitly via Transformer.
explanation_method: Mentions analyzing the user embedding space as a direction for explainability. Ethical considerations section discusses opacity. Self-attention weights could potentially be analyzed (not done).

title: Can Perturbations Help Reduce Investment Risks? Risk-aware Stock Recommendation via Split Variational Adversarial Training
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: SVAT applies split variational adversarial training to risk-aware stock ranking, using generated perturbations to distinguish profitable and risky stocks and estimate risk.
rq2_evaluation: Daily buy-hold-sell (top-k, k=5). Metrics: Investment Return Ratio (IRR), Sharpe Ratio (SR), Maximum Daily Drawdown (MDD). For correlation: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC), Top-k Stocks Difference (TSDk).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Risk quantification via ranking entropy H(xi) derived from VPG-generated perturbations, offering insight into stock risk. Transparency: Low for the core recommendation model (STHAN-SR) and VAE.
financial_domain: Stock Market / Stock Recommendation / Quantitative Finance
contribution: SVAT applies split variational adversarial training to risk-aware stock ranking, using generated perturbations to distinguish profitable and risky stocks and estimate risk.
data_description: Daily stock price data (opening, highest, lowest, closing price, trading volume).
data_source: NASDAQ, NYSE, CASE (normal periods); NASDAQ_08, NYSE_08, CASE_08 (crisis periods). Data sourced from previous work [16], RiceQuant, Yahoo Finance.
data_size: NASDAQ: 1,026 stocks; NYSE: 1,737 stocks; CASE: 4,465 stocks; NASDAQ_08: 656 stocks; NYSE_08: 1,115 stocks; CASE_08: 1,520 stocks. Various time periods for train/validation/test (e.g., NASDAQ Tr: 756 days).
time_characteristics: Daily stock data. Lookback window T (4, 8, 16, 20 days). Normal periods (e.g., 2013-2017) and crisis periods (2002-2008, focusing on 2007-2008).
preprocessing: Input features are historical sequential data (opening, highest, lowest, closing price, trading volume). Specific preprocessing for base features not detailed, but implied for the backbone model.
methods: other (Learning to Rank, Adversarial Training, Deep Learning)
method_details: STHAN-SR ranks stocks. Return-weighted adversarial loss encourages robustness to profitable-stock perturbations and sensitivity to risky-stock perturbations. A VAE-based variational perturbation generator produces risk-related perturbations from latent factors.
architecture: Stock recommendation model (e.g., STHAN-SR) + Variational Perturbation Generator (VPG). VPG has perturbation extractor, posterior encoder, generative decoder, and prior network (MLPs with tanh activation).
training: End-to-end training minimizing a combined loss: L_com = L (recommendation loss) + λ(L_adv (adversarial loss) + L_KL (KL divergence loss)). L_adv is weighted by stock returns. Adam optimizer.
metrics: Investment Return Ratio (IRR), Sharpe Ratio (SR), Maximum Daily Drawdown (MDD). For correlation: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC), Top-k Stocks Difference (TSDk).
baselines: (Buy&Hold, ARIMA, LSTM, GCN, RSR-E, RSR-I, ANN-SVM, STHAN-SR). Also SVAT variants for ablation.
evaluation_protocol: Daily buy-hold-sell (top-k, k=5). Backtesting on 6 datasets (3 normal, 3 crisis) with chronological train/val/test splits. Parameter sensitivity analysis (adversarial constraint ε, backtesting strategy k).
temporal_method: STHAN-SR backbone handles temporal sequences. Input is historical sequential stock data. VPG processes features derived from historical sequences.
temporal_aspects: Historical stock price/return sequences over a lookback window T.
explanation_method: Risk quantification via ranking entropy H(xi) derived from VPG-generated perturbations, offering insight into stock risk.
transparency: Low for the core recommendation model (STHAN-SR) and VAE. Risk quantification provides some interpretability.
implementation: PyTorch; STHAN-SR backbone; VPG with a 2-layer MLP, 128 hidden neurons and tanh. ε=0.001–0.1; α and λ=0.1–1; Adam; 500 epochs; top-k=5.

title: CSRLoan: Cold Start Loan Recommendation with Semantic-Enhanced Neural Matrix Factorization
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: CSRLoan combines statement semantics with dual neural matrix factorization to score loan attractiveness and default risk for cold-start recommendation.
rq2_evaluation: Cold start evaluation on Kiva dataset (Philippines subset). Metrics: HR@K, NDCG@K (K=5, 10).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Semantic embedding from Transformer might offer some insight into statement meaning. Transparency: Low-Moderate (Semantic embeddings somewhat interpretable, NMF is latent factor).
contribution: CSRLoan combines statement semantics with dual neural matrix factorization to score loan attractiveness and default risk for cold-start recommendation.
data_description: Loan application data including applicant features (gender, age, income grade - value; country, repayment - category) and loan project features. Crucially includes applicant's textual statement of purpose. Historical success/default status is used to construct target matrices.
data_source: Kiva crowdfunding dataset (open-source).
data_size: Used Philippines subset. ~850k users, >1M loans total. Split by user for cold start: Train(634k samples, 501k users), Valid(54k samples, 48k users), Test(388k samples, 302k users). Avg statement length ~12-14 words. Details in Table 2.
time_characteristics: Model designed for cold start, thus relies less on historical interaction sequences. Mentions delayed feedback (months/years) as a challenge for loan domain, but does not explicitly model this delay in the recommendation step (focuses on initial statement). Uses statement timestamps implicitly.
preprocessing: Statement Encoding: Pre-training Transformer (2 layers, 7 heads) on statement text using masked language modeling and an "activity" prediction task (default/active/completed). Uses sinusoidal positional encoding. Feature Encoding: Numerical features normalized, categorical features embedded. MLP layers process features.
method_details: A Transformer (2 layers, 7 heads) pretrained on masked language modeling and activity prediction encodes applicant statements. MLPs combine statements, applicant and loan features. Separate NMF heads predict successful-completion and default-risk scores; the final score is o^r_ij + α·o^d_ij.
architecture: Statement Encoder (Transformer) -> Feature Encoder (MLPs) -> Dual Neural Matrix Factorization Module (two separate MLPs predicting recommendation score and default risk score from concatenated user and loan latent vectors). Overall architecture shown in Figure 1.
training: Pre-training the Transformer encoder using masked LM and activity prediction loss (Eq 9). Fine-tuning the entire model (Encoder + Dual NMF) end-to-end using a mixture loss L = L_rec + L_risk (Eq 17), where L_rec and L_risk are MSE losses on the recommendation (R) and default (D) matrices respectively. Adam optimizer used.
metrics: HR@K, NDCG@K (K=5, 10)
baselines: MF-BPR, CML (General Rec); MBR, FAR (Loan Rec). Ablations: NMF (no pre-training, no risk estimation), CSRLoan_pre- (no pre-training), CSRLoan_risk- (no risk estimation).
evaluation_protocol: Cold start evaluation on Kiva dataset (Philippines subset). Split by users (Train/Valid/Test). Compares performance against baselines using HR@K and NDCG@K. Ablation studies conducted to evaluate components. Hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (embedding dim d, mixture loss weight α).
temporal_method: Transformer encoder for statement text, which inherently models word sequences. Sinusoidal positional encoding adds absolute position information. Feature encoding does not explicitly model time, focuses on current applicant/loan features combined with the statement semantic embedding. Designed to handle lack of historical interaction data.
temporal_aspects: Sequence of words within the loan statement. Implicitly captures applicant's current state via features and statement. Does not model user interaction history or loan lifecycle progression explicitly due to cold-start focus.
explanation_method: Semantic embedding from Transformer might offer some insight into statement meaning. Dual NMF provides separate scores for attractiveness and risk. Not explicitly discussed as an explainability technique.
transparency: Low-Moderate (Semantic embeddings somewhat interpretable, NMF is latent factor).
implementation: Transformer: 2 layers, 7 heads; embedding dimension 32; 3-layer MLPs; batch size 128; up to 50 epochs; Adam; α=0.5; 20% token masking. Input features and architecture (Fig. 1) specified.

title: Customer-Category Interest Model: A Graph-Based Collaborative Filtering Model with Applications in Finance
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: GCFCR uses higher-order customer-category graph connectivity to recommend financial-product categories through graph collaborative filtering.
rq2_evaluation: Binary link prediction task (interaction in next 3 months). Metrics: Average Precision Score, Precision, Recall.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: PCA Visualization of category embeddings (Fig 3). Transparency: Moderate.
contribution: GCFCR uses higher-order customer-category graph connectivity to recommend financial-product categories through graph collaborative filtering.
data_description: Customer interactions with 35 product categories over 2 years. Interaction frequency recorded and weighted based on recency/type.
data_source: Real-world financial dataset from J.P. Morgan (proprietary).
data_size: Training: 16,101 customers, 35 categories, ~254k interactions. Testing: 15,495 customers, 35 categories, ~239k interactions. ~9% density. Data covers 2 years.
time_characteristics: Uses 2 years of historical data. Rolling window for train/test (past 12 months predict next 3 months, 6 month gap). Recency explicitly weighted in interaction scores.
preprocessing: Extraction of customer/category interactions. Construction of weighted adjacency matrix based on interaction frequency, recency, and type. Rolling time window split.
method_details: An NGCF-style bipartite graph uses up to 3 message-passing layers, LeakyReLU and element-wise interaction terms. Layer embeddings are concatenated; inner-product scoring with sigmoid predicts customer-category interest.
architecture: Based on NGCF. Initial Embeddings -> Multiple Embedding Propagation Layers (Message Construction -> Aggregation -> Update) -> Concatenation of layer outputs -> Prediction Layer (Inner Product + Sigmoid).
training: Pairwise loss (BPR, BCE, BPR+BCE tested). Negative sampling (1 neg per pos). Adam optimizer. L2 regularization, dropout. Early stopping. Grid search for hyperparameters. Weighted interaction scores used.
metrics: Average Precision Score, Precision, Recall.
baselines: Rule-based, CF-SVD+GBM, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting). Also GCFCR variants (1, 2, 3 layers; different loss functions
evaluation_protocol: Binary link prediction task (interaction in next 3 months). Train/Test split using rolling window (12mo -> 3mo prediction, 6mo gap). Evaluation using Avg Precision, Precision, Recall (threshold 0.5).
temporal_method: Implicit via graph structure capturing historical patterns. Explicit weighting of interactions based on recency. Rolling window setup.
temporal_aspects: Recency of interactions, Historical interaction patterns between customers and categories. High-order temporal relationships implicitly captured by GNN layers.
explanation_method: PCA Visualization of category embeddings (Fig 3). Visualization of similar/dissimilar customer graph neighborhoods (Fig 4).
transparency: Moderate
implementation: TensorFlow; embeddings 16, 32 or 64; Adam; batch size 1024; up to 3 layers; Xavier initialization; negative sampling. Learning rate, L2 and dropout tuned; interaction weighting specified.

contribution: SPGCN separates complementary and substitutable corporate dependencies, combining them through attention for intercorporate investment recommendation.

preprocessing: Construction of bipartite Investment Graph G(I) and multi-relational Corporate Dependency Network G(D) from raw data.

architecture: Initial Embedding (LightGCN) -> SPGCN (Series GCN pathway + Parallel GCN pathway) -> Attentive Aggregation Module -> Final Prediction (Sigmoid of inner product).
training: Supervised Learning. Optimize using cross-entropy loss with negative sampling (implied). Uses Adam optimizer and Xavier initialization. End-to-end training.
metrics: AUC, Recall@K, MAP@K, NDCG@K (K=5, 10, 20).
baselines: (NCF, LightGCN, GRU4Rec, GraphSage, GAT, RGCN). Ablation study: removing G(I), removing G(D), removing Attention, using only Series GCN, using only Parallel GCN.
evaluation_protocol: Task: Predict probability of investor u investing in company i. Evaluation uses standard ranking metrics on the test set (data after 2020). Comparison against baselines and ablation variants. Case studies and visualizations reported.
temporal_method: Primarily graph-based. Time used for chronological train/test split. GRU4Rec used as a temporal baseline.
temporal_aspects: Investment date used for train/test split. GRU4Rec baseline captures sequence. SPGCN itself does not explicitly model time dynamics.
explanation_method: Decomposition into interpretable complementary/substitutable features (S_i, P_i). Attentive Aggregation module provides weights (alpha^S, alpha^P, alpha^R) showing relative importance of features for a given prediction. Visualization of feature similarities (Fig 3). Case studies explaining recommendations (Fig 4).
transparency: Moderate (GNNs have some opacity, but the explicit decomposition and attention weights aid interpretation).
implementation: PyTorch and DGL; 2 LightGCN/SPGCN layers; embedding dimension 64; Adam and Xavier initialization. Architecture in Fig. 2 and Section IV.

Calculating similarity matrices (Cosine, Jaccobi). Normalizing indicators. Combining scores.

RSI, OBV and support/resistance scores use divergence, peak, trend and boundary routines (Algorithms 4–7). architecture: Two main modules: Recommendation Engine (calculates similarity scores, eigen decomposition, final recommendation), Data Provider (calculates technical analysis scores, provides data). Backend uses Neo4j graph database. Implemented in Scala with Apache Spark.
training: Not traditional ML training. Eigen decomposition performed initially. Eigenvalues/vectors updated incrementally using formulas from [7] (Algo 3). Technical indicators calculated based on rules and historical data. Recommendation involves calculating similarities and TA scores, then combining them.
metrics: Precision, Recall (vs. benchmarks based on relevancy threshold). Accuracy (for TA score prediction vs future price movement).
baselines: Compared against graph embedding methods LINE and DeepWalk using Precision/Recall
evaluation_protocol: 1. Compare against LINE/DeepWalk using Precision/Recall based on % of shared stocks between recommended investors and target investor (relevancy threshold 20% used in Table 5). 2. Evaluate the system's stock score accuracy by comparing predicted trend (Growth/Loss/Same based on score > 50+Δ, < 50-Δ, or in between) against actual price movement at t+1, t+2, t+3 days for Δ=0.03 and Δ=0.01 (Tables 7, 8). Tested on 15 random stocks.
temporal_method: Technical analysis indicators (RSI, OBV) calculated on historical price/volume data (e.g., 14 periods). Eigen decomposition updates use previous iteration's state. TA score combination is static. System designed for real-time updates.
temporal_aspects: Stock price movements, trends, volume changes, support/resistance levels. Investor similarity potentially changes over time implicitly via stock possession updates in graph.
explanation_method: Not reported.
transparency: Low
implementation: Scala 2.12, Neo4j, Apache Spark; divergence uses 2 recent peaks; peak buffer 7 and thresholds ±0.03; RSI uses 3 peaks with weights 25,5,1; boundary buffer 7. Eigensystem/update Algorithms 1–3; ConcurrentHashMap parallelization.

Agent observes state (x(t)), selects action (k(t)) via TS+LR based on sampled parameters, receives reward (r(t)), updates posterior distributions of LR parameters (μ(t+1), λ(t+1)). Uses logistic regression as the core predictive model. Algorithm 2 provides detailed procedure.
training: Online learning. Parameter updates (μ, λ for logistic regression) are performed after each interaction using Bayesian update rules derived via Laplace approximation. metrics: Cumulative Regret, Precision, Recall, F1-score, AUC, nDCG, MAP.
baselines: Contextual MABs: Linear TS, Linear UCB, Linear Greedy, Kernel TS, Kernel UCB; Tree models: Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost; Others: Logistic Regression, KNN

temporal_aspects: Evolving investor preferences (captured by the dynamically updated mean vector μ / priority vector μ-hat of the logistic regression model). Real-time interaction feedback loop.
explanation_method: Derives an investor's priority vector (normalized μ-hat from logistic regression parameters) to explain the relative importance of different attributes (contextual features) in the recommendation decision (Section 3.2, Table 6).

implementation: Algorithms 1–4; Bayesian/Laplace formulation; Theorems 1–2 with appendix proofs; attributes in Table 3; updates (Eqs. 3, 4, 9); z-score standardization.

title: KiRTi: A Blockchain-Based Credit Recommender System for Financial Institutions
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: KiRTi combines blockchain histories, LSTM credit scores and smart contracts for loan recommendations, with repayment feedback updating the model.
rq2_evaluation: Train/Test split (80:20) on German Credit dataset. Metrics: Accuracy, F-measure, Error rate, Precision, Recall, True Negative Rate (TNR), False Positive Rate (FPR), ROC/AUC, Computation Cost (CC), Communication Cost (CCM), Scalability (Block addition time).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Explanation method not reported. Transparency: Low (LSTM is black-box); High (Blockchain data/transactions are transparent).
financial_domain: Credit Scoring, Loan Recommendation, Lending Operations
contribution: KiRTi combines blockchain histories, LSTM credit scores and smart contracts for loan recommendations, with repayment feedback updating the model.
data_description: PB historical transactions, current assets, liabilities, loan purpose, credit/lending history, job type, bank balance, education, repayment/default history, etc. Data stored as time-series on blockchain. Used German Credit Dataset for evaluation.
data_source: German Credit Dataset (UCI Repository).
data_size: 1000 credit histories (700 good, 300 bad) from German Credit Dataset. 20 attributes.
time_characteristics: Data stored as time-series sequence on blockchain. LSTM models temporal dependencies. Real-time feedback loop updates model based on repayment/default events. SCs automate time-bound processes.
preprocessing: Fetches historical data (H[TR]) from blockchain. Data vectorized (VM). Normalized. Split into Train/Test (80:20). Missing values handled (mean imputation). Random forest used for initial classification (in experiments).
method_details: An LSTM processes borrower-history vectors to produce scores {Rs,Cs} from lender interactions and assets/liabilities. Repayment/default indicators v and t update weights; smart contracts execute loan setup and repayment under predefined rules.
architecture: Blockchain stores data -> LSTM model retrieves data -> LSTM generates credit score {Rs, Cs} -> Lending algorithms use scores -> Smart Contracts execute agreements -> Feedback (repayment/default outcomes) updates LSTM weights. (See Fig 1, Fig 3 for LSTM cell).
training: Supervised training of LSTM on historical (German Credit) data. Continuous learning via a real-time feedback loop that adjusts LSTM edge-weights based on repayment success (v=1, t=1) or default (v=0, t=0). Trained using gradient descent, backpropagation.
metrics: Accuracy, F-measure, Error rate, Precision, Recall, True Negative Rate (TNR), False Positive Rate (FPR), ROC/AUC, Computation Cost (CC), Communication Cost (CCM), Scalability (Block addition time).
baselines: Accuracy vs GBDT [17], SVM [18], CNN+belief [19]. CC/CCM vs Odelu [23], Kabra [1]
evaluation_protocol: Train/Test split (80:20) on German Credit dataset. Calculation of classification metrics. ROC curve analysis. Formal verification of Smart Contract using Mythril. Comparison of computational and communication costs against benchmarks. Scalability analysis based on block addition time vs number of transactions.
temporal_method: LSTM network processing time-series data. Blockchain stores data chronologically. Real-time feedback loop based on repayment/default events (boolean indicators v, t) updates LSTM edge weights.
temporal_aspects: PB's historical financial data as sequences. Captures long-term dependencies in credit history. Models impact of recent repayment/default events on creditworthiness via feedback loop.
explanation_method: Not reported.
transparency: Low (LSTM is black-box); High (Blockchain data/transactions are transparent).
implementation: German Credit data; Spark 2.4.4, scikit-learn 0.22.1, Solidity 0.5.11/Remix; 12 GB NVIDIA GPU; VectorAssembler. LSTM maxlen 150, units 128, dropout 0.267, batch size 32 (Table I). Algorithms 1–4; Mythril verification; cost calculations.

title: Large-scale Recommendation for Portfolio Optimization
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: A hybrid MPT-CF recommender reranks collaborative stock candidates by holdings-based utility and investor risk aversion, using an analytic scoring derivation.
rq2_evaluation: Domain expert evaluation study. Metrics: Qualitative expert evaluation. Friedman test, Nemenyi post-hoc test, Logit regression used to analyze expert preferences between recommendation lists.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: MPT provides risk-return rationale. Transparency: Moderate.
financial_domain: Stock Recommendation, Portfolio Optimization, Retail Investment (Online Brokers)
contribution: A hybrid MPT-CF recommender reranks collaborative stock candidates by holdings-based utility and investor risk aversion, using an analytic scoring derivation.
data_description: User portfolio holdings (daily market value snapshots), derived user interaction history (holding matrix R), user risk aversion estimates, stock historical returns.
data_source: Historical trading data from a brokerage firm (users, holdings). Stock data from Tokyo Stock Exchange and Nagoya Stock Exchange.
data_size: "few hundreds of thousands of users", 3,714 stocks. Evaluation used 20 actual user portfolios.
time_characteristics: Daily portfolio snapshots. MPT uses historical returns with exponential weighting (EWMA). CF uses holding history over interval TR (>= 6 mo) and recent state over TW (e.g., day/week/month). 2 years of data used.
preprocessing: Holdings form binary matrix R and normalized-value matrix W. EWMA estimates µ and Σ; γ is the geometric mean of inferred daily optimal risk aversion. Item co-counts and transitions form CF matrices.
method_details: Item-item CF derives co-occurrence/Markov scores from holdings and selects top-k candidates. MPT utility combines expected return, variance and risk aversion γ to rerank them (Algorithm 1); Eq. 9 gives an analytic score.
architecture: Pipeline: Estimate Risk Aversion -> Compute MPT Utility (YMPT) -> Compute CF Scores (YCF) -> Hybrid Re-ranking.
training: MPT parameters estimated via EWMA on historical returns. CF matrices derived from historical user holdings. User risk aversion estimated from historical portfolio choices. No iterative training of a predictive model.
metrics: Qualitative expert evaluation. Friedman test, Nemenyi post-hoc test, Logit regression used to analyze expert preferences between recommendation lists.
baselines: Random, MPT-only, UserCF-only
evaluation_protocol: Domain expert evaluation study. 3 experts evaluated top-20 recommendations from 4 methods for 20 user portfolios with varying risk aversion levels in a two-step unlabeled, randomized process. Statistical analysis of choices made.
temporal_method: MPT uses Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) for returns/risk. CF uses historical holding data over periods TR and TW.
temporal_aspects: Time-varying stock returns/risk (via MPT/EWMA). User's historical holdings/familiarity (via CF). Recent portfolio state (via CF matrix W). Investment time horizon (via MPT/EWMA parameters and TW period).
explanation_method: MPT provides risk-return rationale. Aims for "clearly explainable investment agenda". Explains recommendation based on individual stock's impact on portfolio utility (Fig 2).
transparency: Moderate
implementation: MPT equations (1, 2, 8, 9), CF equations (6–7) and Algorithm 1; risk-aversion estimation and EWMA described. Python is implied rather than explicitly confirmed.

title: Learning Dynamic Insurance Recommendations from Users' Click Sessions
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: Proposes an LSTM autoencoder for insurance click sessions and a second LSTM for cross-session recommendation under sparse purchase feedback.
rq2_evaluation: Preliminary work: Train/Val/Test split (80/10/10). Metrics: Preliminary work: Balanced Accuracy, Precision, Recall, AUC. (Metrics for the main proposed framework not fully detailed/evaluated in the paper).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Mentions plan to study interpretable ML techniques (ICE, LIME, SHAP) as future work to explain recommendations. Transparency: Low (Proposed LSTM models are black-box).
contribution: Proposes an LSTM autoencoder for insurance click sessions and a second LSTM for cross-session recommendation under sparse purchase feedback.
data_description: User click sessions (sequences of clicks with timestamps) from an insurance website. Purchase intent is the target variable in preliminary experiments.
data_source: Real-world dataset from Alka Forsikring (Danish insurance company).
data_size: Preliminary work data: 433,141 sessions, 3,356,183 clicks, 56,252 sessions with purchase.
time_characteristics: Data collected May 2017 - April 2018. Explicitly models sequences of sessions over time. Aims to capture users' dynamic needs evolving over time. Considers session recency as a future work topic.
preprocessing: Session definition (clicks < 30 mins apart). Split into train/validation/test (80/10/10). Preliminary work tested feature engineering and sequential feature extraction. Proposed work uses LSTM autoencoder to learn representations directly.
method_details: An LSTM autoencoder represents within-session clicks; another LSTM models the session sequence. Preliminary purchase-intent experiments compare LSTM and FFNN models on engineered features.
architecture: Two-stage LSTM architecture (Fig 2): 1) LSTM Autoencoder for session representation learning. 2) LSTM network processes sequence of encoded sessions (st) to predict output (ot).
training: Autoencoder trained to reconstruct click sequences. Second LSTM trained (presumably supervised) on sequences of session representations to predict next items/purchase intent. Details on loss functions not reported for the proposed framework.
metrics: Preliminary work: Balanced Accuracy, Precision, Recall, AUC. (Metrics for the main proposed framework not fully detailed/evaluated in the paper).
baselines: Preliminary work compared sequential click model vs engineered features model vs demographic model. (Proposed work not benchmarked yet).
evaluation_protocol: Preliminary work: Train/Val/Test split (80/10/10). Evaluated purchase intent prediction within current session. Ablation study on click order importance. Proposed framework described conceptually but evaluation results not presented.
temporal_method: LSTM Autoencoder captures intra-session temporal dynamics. Second LSTM models inter-session temporal dynamics (sequence of sessions over time). Aims to capture evolving user needs.
temporal_aspects: Sequential order of clicks within sessions. Sequential order of user sessions over time. Evolution of user needs/preferences.
explanation_method: Mentions plan to study interpretable ML techniques (ICE, LIME, SHAP) as future work to explain recommendations.
transparency: Low (Proposed LSTM models are black-box).
implementation: Proposed LSTM-autoencoder/LSTM framework (Fig. 2); preliminary LSTM/FFNN experiments and data described. Proposed-network parameters not reported.

title: Learning Recommendations from User Actions in the Item-poor Insurance Domain
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: Cross-session RNNs use multiple user actions to recommend insurance products despite sparse purchases; a public dataset is reported.
rq2_evaluation: Train/Test split (last 10% purchases for test, 90% for train). Metrics: HR@k, Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR@k, MAP@k (k=3 used mainly, k=1-5 shown in Fig 7).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Plans to investigate explainability techniques and generate user-readable explanations as future work. Transparency: Low (RNN models are black-box).
contribution: Cross-session RNNs use multiple user actions to recommend insurance products despite sparse purchases; a public dataset is reported.
data_description: User clickstream data from an insurance website: sequences of sessions, each containing sequences of actions (timestamp, action section, action object, action type - click/start/act/complete). Also user demographics (age, employment, income etc.) and purchase history (portfolio) used for baselines. Target is user's next purchase event (items can be new products or additional coverage).
data_source: Real-world dataset from a commercial insurance vendor (anonymized), made publicly available by authors.
data_size: ~44K users, 16 items, ~54K purchase events, ~117K sessions, ~1.26M actions. Data spans Oct 2018 - Sep 2020.
time_characteristics: Models sequences of user sessions chronologically. Target action (purchase) occurs after the sequence of input sessions. Uses an inactivity threshold (10 days) estimated from data to define relevant "recent" sessions. Session length truncated (max 30 actions). Max 7 sessions per user kept.
preprocessing: Removal of low-frequency items/actions (<0.1%). Removal of consecutive repeated actions. Removal of short sessions (<3 actions). Session truncation (max 30 actions). User history truncation (max 7 sessions). Estimation of inter-session inactivity threshold (10 days) using Gaussian Mixture Model on log-scaled inter-session times. Post-filtering recommendations based on product prerequisites.
method_details: Cross-sessions Encode max-pools within sessions before a GRU; Concat feeds concatenated actions to a GRU; Auto uses LSTM-autoencoder session embeddings before a GRU. Sigmoid outputs predict purchases; hybrid FFNN variants add demographics.
architecture: GRU-based RNNs. Architectures vary based on session encoding (Encode: MaxPool -> GRU; Concat: GRU on flattened sequence; Auto: LSTM Autoencoder -> GRU). Autoencoder uses single GRU layer. Final dense layer with Sigmoid. Hybrid model concatenates GRU output with FFNN output from demographics. (See Figs 2, 3, 4, 5).
training: Supervised learning. Multi-label classification task. Loss function is sum of binary cross-entropy over all items (Eq 5). Autoencoder trained using categorical cross-entropy loss. Adam optimizer. Early stopping based on validation loss. Grid search for hyperparameter tuning (batch size, units, dropout).
metrics: HR@k, Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR@k, MAP@k (k=3 used mainly, k=1-5 shown in Fig 7).
baselines: Random, Popular, SVD, Demographic (FFNN), GRU4REC, GRU4REC Concat, SKNN_E, SKNN_EB
evaluation_protocol: Train/Test split (last 10% purchases for test, 90% for train). Validation split (last 10% of training). Uses cutoff k=3. Statistical significance testing (McNemar's, ANOVA). Ablation study on number of sessions/actions used. Ablation study on removing different action types/sections/objects. Analysis of session order importance via shuffling. Comparison of different cross-session model variants. Comparison with hybrid demographic models.
temporal_method: RNN (GRU) applied to sequences of sessions. Explores different ways to encode/process sessions (Encode, Concat, Auto). LSTM Autoencoder used in one variant. Explicitly models dependencies across sessions. Estimated session inactivity threshold (10 days) used to group relevant sessions.
temporal_aspects: Sequence of user actions within sessions. Sequence of sessions over time. Captures dynamic user preferences implicitly through session sequences. Different action types (clicks, form interactions) used as temporal signals.
explanation_method: Plans to investigate explainability techniques and generate user-readable explanations as future work.
transparency: Low (RNN models are black-box).
implementation: Python 3.7.4; TensorFlow 2.6.0; Adam; 2-layer networks. Batch size 32–128, units 64–512, dropout 0.2–0.4 (Table 3); up to 6 hours training; session encoders and preprocessing described.
open_science: Code and dataset release reported via GitHub; access unverified.

title: Learning to recommend via random walk with profile of loan and lender in P2P lending
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: RRWP combines lender/loan profiles with a hybrid random walk for two-way P2P recommendations under sparsity and cold start.
rq2_evaluation: 5-fold cross-validation. Metrics: HR@K, NDCG@K, Precision@K, Recall@K (typically K=20).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Profile components (e.g., lender risk preference, loan predicted risk) provide some level of interpretability. Transparency: Moderate.
target_users: Lenders (investors) and Loans (borrowers/loan applications) on P2P platforms
contribution: RRWP combines lender/loan profiles with a hybrid random walk for two-way P2P recommendations under sparsity and cold start.
data_description: P2P loan data: Loan attributes (Amount, LendRate, Category etc.), borrower attributes (Credit, DebtToIncome etc.), lender investment history (who invested in which loan, amount), loan outcome (completed, defaulted, expired etc.). Lender profile includes derived social/psychological features (based on demographics) and historical investment patterns (avg risk, return, popularity).
data_source: Public Prosper marketplace dataset (used in 3 versions: overall, Prosper1 focusing on ~$10k loans, Prosper2 on ~$20-25k loans).
data_size: Overall dataset size not specified, but subsets Prosper1 (2774 loans, ~0.6M records) and Prosper2 (1469 loans, ~0.66M records) used, covering significant portion of original Prosper dataset (~2.6M records).
time_characteristics: Uses historical investment data to build lender purchase-based profile. Uses historical loan outcomes to train risk prediction model. Random walk performed on a static graph snapshot representing these historical patterns.
preprocessing: Building loan profile (return=repayment rate; risk=logistic regression on loan+borrower features; popularity=logistic regression). Building lender profile (social/psychological via fuzzy rules based on demographics; historical via weighted avg of invested loans' profiles). Constructing hybrid graph (lender-loan interaction edges, lender-lender similarity edges based on profile cosine sim, loan-loan similarity edges based on profile cosine sim). Normalizing similarity matrices. Defining transition probabilities for random walk based on profiles/status (Eq 5-12).
method_details: Loan profiles contain return, risk and popularity; lender profiles add social and psychological attributes. Investment and cosine-similarity graphs form a hybrid network. Type-, funding- and pledge-dependent transitions with restart φ/λ yield stationary rankings of loans for lenders and lenders for loans.
architecture: Profile Modeling Module -> Hybrid Graph Construction Module -> Recommendation Module (Random Walk). (See Fig 4).
training: Logistic Regression models trained for loan risk & popularity using historical data (Vp). Fuzzy rules defined for social/psychological lender profile. Historical purchase profile aggregated. Random walk parameters (restart prob φ, λ; transition weights α, β based on ω, ξ) tuned via grid search/sensitivity analysis (Fig 7). Random walk itself is an iterative process, not parameter training.
metrics: HR@K, NDCG@K, Precision@K, Recall@K (typically K=20).
baselines: Graph-based: Pixie, RecWalk, RWH. Deep Learning: NCF, NGCF. Also includes ablation study with RRWP variants: RRWP_1 (bipartite only), RRWP_2 (+loan profile), RRWP_3 (+lender soc/psy profile), RRWP_4 (+lender hist. profile)
evaluation_protocol: 5-fold cross-validation. 80/20 train/test split. Evaluation performed on Prosper1 and Prosper2 datasets for both lender and loan recommendation tasks. Parameter sensitivity analyzed (Fig 7). Component contribution analyzed via RRWP variants. Profile modeling validity checked via correlations (Fig 10, 11, 12). Statistical significance tested (dependent t-test). Running time comparison (Fig 9).
temporal_method: Aggregate historical data used to build static profiles (lender purchase history, loan risk/popularity models). Random Walk process itself does not explicitly model time decay or sequence order.
temporal_aspects: Historical investment patterns (aggregated into lender profile). Historical loan success/failure (used for risk model training). Loan funding status (dynamic aspect used in transition probability β).
explanation_method: Profile components (e.g., lender risk preference, loan predicted risk) provide some level of interpretability. Analysis in Fig 10-12 attempts to validate profile reasonableness based on financial theory.
transparency: Moderate. Profile construction logic is explained. Random walk is somewhat black-box but operates on interpretable graph structure.
implementation: Logistic/fuzzy profile models; random-walk transition/restart equations (5–15); hybrid graph (Fig. 3), architecture (Fig. 4), parameter sensitivity (Fig. 7), ω/ξ/φ/λ settings and evaluation described.

title: Leveraging Unstructured Data to Improve Customer Engagement and Revenue in Financial Institutions: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach to Personalized Transaction Recommendations
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: Combines structured and transaction-text features with deep Q-learning to recommend credit cards under a user-satisfaction reward.
rq2_evaluation: Evaluation on test set using standard classification/ranking metrics. Metrics: AUC-ROC, Recall, Precision, F1 Score, NDCG. For Q-Learning component: Success Rate, Average Reward, Average Steps, Exploration Rate, Convergence Time, Policy Entropy. Qualitative Analysis.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Qualitative analysis mentioned. Transparency: Low.
contribution: Combines structured and transaction-text features with deep Q-learning to recommend credit cards under a user-satisfaction reward.
data_description: Customer demographics (age, gender, income), card transaction data (amount, date, time, location, merchant category code, retailer name), unstructured transaction descriptions.
data_source: Public dataset: IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection.
data_size: Contains over 590,000 transactions from ~1.5 million anonymized customers over a six-month period. Split into 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test.
time_characteristics: RNN (LSTM) used to capture temporal dynamics of customer transactions. Transaction history used as part of the state in RL. Recency and frequency mentioned as potential temporal features extracted during preprocessing.
preprocessing: Data cleaning, feature engineering (temporal features), one-hot encoding for categorical features. NLP techniques (tokenization, stemming, stop-word removal) on transaction descriptions. Use of pre-trained word embeddings for CNN input. Padding sequences to fixed length.
method_details: CNN features represent customer demographics; an LSTM models transaction histories and NLP processes descriptions. An MLP combines the features into the DQN state; Q-learning selects credit-card recommendations to maximize expected satisfaction.
architecture: Input (Demographics, Transactions) -> CNN Feature Extractor (Demographics) & RNN Temporal Modeler (Transactions) -> MLP Feature Combination -> DQN Agent (Policy Learning) -> Output Recommendations (Credit Card Offers). DQN uses a two-layer fully connected network. Hybrid model architecture combines CNN and RNN outputs.
training: Supervised training for CNN/RNN feature extractors (implied). Reinforcement Learning (DQN) training using experience replay and target networks to learn the optimal recommendation policy based on maximizing expected rewards. Trained for 100 episodes, 590k transactions/episode. Uses Adam optimizer, epsilon-greedy exploration strategy.
metrics: AUC-ROC, Recall, Precision, F1 Score, NDCG. For Q-Learning component: Success Rate, Average Reward, Average Steps, Exploration Rate, Convergence Time, Policy Entropy. Qualitative Analysis.
baselines: Logistic Regression - Model A, CNN - Model B). Ablation study (with/without RNN and CNN components - Table IV
evaluation_protocol: Evaluation on test set using standard classification/ranking metrics. Comparison against baseline models. Evaluation of Q-learning component performance. Qualitative analysis of generated recommendations for 100 random customers.
temporal_method: RNN (specifically LSTM)
temporal_aspects: Temporal dynamics of customer transaction sequences. Long-term dependencies in transaction data. Uses transaction history as part of the RL state.
explanation_method: Qualitative analysis mentioned. Transaction descriptions (processed by NLP) provide context. RL learns based on reward signals reflecting alignment with user preferences/behavior. DQN itself is black-box.
transparency: Low
implementation: CNN/RNN steps (Algorithms 1–2); LSTM; TensorFlow/PyTorch DQN with 2 hidden layers of 64 ReLU units and linear output. Adam learning rate 0.001; Q-learning rate 0.01; discount 0.99; ε-greedy exploration.

title: LFFI-H: A Recommendation System Suitable for Crowdfunding Platform
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: LFFI-H combines latent factors, investment-category history and a multilayer perceptron for crowdfunding recommendations.
rq2_evaluation: Offline evaluation using 80/20 train/test split on the Kiva dataset. Metrics: AUC, Cross-Entropy.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Explanation method not reported. Transparency: Low (MF part provides some latent factor insight, but MLP is black-box).
contribution: LFFI-H combines latent factors, investment-category history and a multilayer perceptron for crowdfunding recommendations.
data_description: User attributes (lenderID, loan-count, historical category preference vector), Project attributes (loanID, funded-amount, sector, lender-count, bonus-credit-eligibility), User-project investment interactions.
data_source: Kiva.org (http://kiva.org/) public dataset (via Zhao et al. [18])
data_size: 5,486 users, 4,649 projects (after cleaning).
time_characteristics: Uses historical investment records to compute a static user category preference feature vector. Does not explicitly model temporal sequences or dynamics beyond this feature engineering step.
preprocessing: Data cleaning (remove users < 4 investments, remove incorrect fields). One-hot encoding for categorical features. Standardization for numerical features. Creation of user historical investment category preference vector (dimension = number of categories, value = ratio of investments in that category).
method_details: User/item latent vectors and category-preference features enter a ReLU MLP with sigmoid investment prediction. MF features are introduced at a shallower DNN layer.
architecture: Two-part: Latent Factor Decomposition (MF) module + MLP module. MF features are input to a shallower MLP layer compared to standard DNN approaches. User category preference vector is concatenated with MF features and other basic features before MLP input (Fig 1).
training: Supervised binary classification. Trained end-to-end using Cross-Entropy loss. RMSprop optimizer.
metrics: AUC, Cross-Entropy
baselines: RF, GBDT+LR, FM, DeepFM, LCW, LFFI (own variant without hierarchy)
evaluation_protocol: Offline evaluation using 80/20 train/test split on the Kiva dataset. Compares AUC and cross-entropy against baselines. Includes hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (latent factor dimension k, number of DNN layers).
temporal_method: Feature engineering from user historical investment data (creates static category preference vector).
temporal_aspects: User historical investment category preferences (aggregated into a static feature).
explanation_method: Not reported.
transparency: Low (MF part provides some latent factor insight, but MLP is black-box).
implementation: Architecture (Fig. 1); cross-entropy; RMSprop learning rate 0.001; batch size 128; ReLU/sigmoid; preprocessing and latent-dimension/layer-count tests described.

title: Maximizing Customer Lifetime Value using Stacked Neural Networks: An Insurance Industry Application
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: Stacks purchase-history recommendation and neural survival analysis to select insurance products using predicted customer lifetime value.
rq2_evaluation: Evaluation uses case studies on specific users from the dataset. Metrics: Visualizations (Survival Curves, Defection Risk, CLV Maximization plots per user). Comparison between Stage I recommendation (MaxSurv) and final recommendation (MaxCLV) for example users (Table I). No standard RS metrics (Precision, Recall, NDCG).
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: No dedicated explanation method reported. Transparency: Low.
contribution: Stacks purchase-history recommendation and neural survival analysis to select insurance products using predicted customer lifetime value.
data_description: Transactional data (purchase history), item features, user features (implied). Data includes subscription start/end times, item features embeddings, user purchase sequence.
data_source: Data from a large Australian insurance company serving small-and-medium enterprises (SMEs).
data_size: 18 different items, 19,174 customers, 173,127 transactions.
time_characteristics: Data spans 2007-2019. Models sequential purchase history. Uses time embeddings (sinusoidal). Stage II models time-to-event (survival analysis). Represents user subscription intervals and purchase times.
preprocessing: Cleaning and transformation. Creating purchase history sequences (Xu). Generating item embeddings (d-dimensional).
methods: Hybrid, Other (Deep Learning, Sequential, Survival Analysis)
method_details: Self-attention encodes purchase histories; collaborative metric learning scores candidates by Euclidean user/item distance. A neural survival model predicts log risk after adding each candidate; pairwise risk comparisons select the item with the highest predicted CLV.
architecture: Stacked two-stage architecture. Stage I: Self-Attention + CML. Stage II: Neural Network for Survival Analysis.
training: Stage I: Minimize pairwise ranking loss (BPR-like) with L2 regularization. Stage II: Minimize average negative log partial likelihood of survival model with L2 regularization using gradient descent.
metrics: Visualizations (Survival Curves, Defection Risk, CLV Maximization plots per user). Comparison between Stage I recommendation (MaxSurv) and final recommendation (MaxCLV) for example users (Table I). No standard RS metrics (Precision, Recall, NDCG).
baselines: Compares the final CLV-optimized recommendation against the initial recommendation from the self-attention model (Stage I).
evaluation_protocol: Evaluation uses case studies on specific users from the dataset. Demonstrates how the recommended item changes when optimizing for CLV vs. standard sequential recommendation. Plots survival curves and risk profiles for different recommended items.
temporal_method: Self-Attention processes sequential purchase history. Sinusoidal time embeddings are added to input. Neural Network based Survival Analysis explicitly models time-to-event (customer churn/defection).
temporal_aspects: User purchase sequence over time. Time step information via embeddings. Customer lifetime/time-to-churn via survival analysis.
explanation_method: No dedicated explanation method reported. The REC matrix compares predicted product risks for CLV; attention and survival components remain opaque.
transparency: Low
implementation: Self-attention, CML and survival architecture; 1×1 projections, softmax and sinusoidal time embeddings; pairwise-ranking and negative-log-partial-likelihood losses; REC matrix described. Survival-network architecture and hyperparameters incomplete.

title: Modeling and analysis of a stock-based collaborative filtering algorithm for the Chinese stock market
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: A stock-based CF strategy ranks Chinese stocks using lagged cross-stock price correlations and examines inter-industry transmission.
rq2_evaluation: Backtesting an investment strategy on historical data (2014-2018). Metrics: Investment strategy performance metrics: Total Returns, Annualized Return, Maximum Drawdown, Alpha, Beta, Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, Information Ratio, Algorithm Volatility.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Market-level analysis of inter-industry transmission effects (Section 5, Figs 6-9). Transparency: Moderate.
contribution: A stock-based CF strategy ranks Chinese stocks using lagged cross-stock price correlations and examines inter-industry transmission.
data_description: Daily stock prices, market index data (CSI 800), industry classifications (CITIC industry index).
data_source: Chinese stock market data via JoinQuant platform. CSI 800 constituent stocks. CITIC industry indices.
data_size: 800 stocks in pool. Training period 2009-2013 (for period optimization). Backtesting period 2014-2018. Industry analysis period 2004-2016.
time_characteristics: Daily prices aggregated over defined short (optimized: 50 days) and long (optimized: 15 short periods) periods. Captures lagged correlation (transmission effect) between stock movements (current target stock vs. previous related stock). Uses recent short-term performance for ranking.
preprocessing: Calculation of relative stock movement within short periods (Eq 9). Construction of movement vectors over long periods. Calculation of Pearson correlation coefficients (Eq 10). Selection of top correlated stocks. Calculation of ranking index (Eq 12).
method_details: Pearson correlations link a target stock's current long-period movement to another stock's previous-period movement. The top 5 positively related stocks form its reference group; recent group performance ranks targets, and the top 5 are bought.
architecture: Algorithmic pipeline based on statistical calculations (correlation, ranking). Not a typical ML/DL architecture.
training: Period optimization (finding optimal short/long period lengths) based on maximizing strategy net value on a training dataset. No explicit model training; relies on calculating correlations from historical data.
metrics: Investment strategy performance metrics: Total Returns, Annualized Return, Maximum Drawdown, Alpha, Beta, Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, Information Ratio, Algorithm Volatility.
baselines: Comparison against CSI 800 benchmark index. Comparison against 3 Chinese industry wheel moving funds.
evaluation_protocol: Backtesting an investment strategy on historical data (2014-2018). Strategy: Buy top 5 ranked stocks, hold for one short period (50 days), sell, repeat. Period lengths (short=50 days, long=15 short periods) optimized on separate data (2009-2013). Analysis of strategy performance with varying period lengths. Analysis of inter-industry transmission effects using average correlation coefficients.
temporal_method: Explicit definition and calculation of short (50 days) and long (15*50 days) periods. Uses lagged Pearson correlation between time-series movement vectors (current vs. previous long period). Ranks based on performance in the last short period.
temporal_aspects: Stock price movement patterns over time (short/long periods). Lagged relationships ("transmission effect") between stocks. Relative strength based on recent (last short period) momentum of related stocks.
explanation_method: Market-level analysis of inter-industry transmission effects (Section 5, Figs 6-9). Ranking index provides a relative strength score. The CF mechanism itself is based on statistical correlation.

metrics: Accuracy (hit rate vs actual investments), Profit (avg. portfolio return considering defaults), Risk (std. dev. of interest rates in portfolio). Hypervolume (HV) for comparing MOEA performance.

temporal_method: Historical data used to derive static preferences/weights: (1) Lender's historical average expected return (Ei) used in CFM calculation. (2) Historical final loan state (utility) used to weight initial resources in ProbS(Weight) for WPR calculation.
temporal_aspects: Lender's historical risk preference (via Ei). Past loan performance/utility (via ProbS(Weight) weights). Does not model the sequence or timing of investments or market changes dynamically.

title: Recommendation of A-Share Stock-Based Graph Dual-Attention Self-Learning

implementation: Graph rules, attention equations, relation loss, Algorithm 1, split and selected hyperparameters documented. Graph/split isolation, folds and pretrained checkpoint IDs are incompletely specified.

method_details: Coefficient updates remain near prior estimates subject to click constraints. ICEA resolves infeasible comparisons; ε sets the mix of random and greedy items.
architecture: Fund pool, recommendation list, simulated click feedback, utility update, next list.
training: Online optimization after each interaction. Fixed epsilon in {0,0.1,0.3,0.5,0.8,1}. No neural-network training.
metrics: Single Utility Difference upper bound, Recommendation Fitness, cumulative reward accounting for interaction cost.
baselines: Epsilon settings, including pure greedy epsilon=0 and random exploration epsilon=1.
evaluation_protocol: Simulation over 3,000 interactions. Four known utilities allow estimation-error and long-run reward comparisons.
temporal_method: Incremental preference learning and exploration/exploitation.
temporal_aspects: Click-sequence accumulation across interactions. Preset true customer utility stays fixed within an experiment.
explanation_method: Explicit linear utility weights. No dedicated user explanation interface.
transparency: Estimated utility and optimization constraints inspectable. No explanation user study.
implementation: Mathematical programs, ICEA pseudocode, ε-greedy algorithm and simulation settings documented.
open_science: Code release not reported; public source data, with study data available on request.

title: Multilingual BERT-based Classification and Recommendation Model for Supporting Innovation Finance Decisions
rq1_methods_financial_adaptation: Curriculum/expert-reinforced BERT predicts firm innovation product codes for finance screening; classification scope, no investor-to-product suitability.
rq2_evaluation: Label top-k accuracy, curriculum ablations and separate expert rank agreement on newer firms; split/checkpoint ambiguities; no investment outcomes.
rq3_explainability_trust_suitability: Human expert semantic review and ranked code confidence; no explanation-faithfulness, investor trust or suitability study.
contribution: Predicts Innovation-Growth Intelligence System product codes for innovation-finance screening.
data_description: Innovation-growth product taxonomy/manual, KSIC crosswalk, innovation-finance records, Technology Credit Bureau records, firm profiles and expert-generated keyword phrases.
data_source: Korean innovation-finance/IGS data described in Table 1; firm/product descriptions and expert annotation.
data_size: Table 1: manual 360 codes; KSIC 3,433 records; finance 80,916 firms; TCB 64,765 entries; firm profiles 75,011 firms. These sources may overlap. Model: nine themes, 46 subcategories, 284 codes. Approximately 20,000 synthetic phrases; expert holdout 785 firms.
time_characteristics: Holdout: new firm records April–June 2024 excluded from training. Training-source periods not fully specified.
preprocessing: WordPiece/[CLS] text encoding; manual/crosswalk alignment; synthetic phrases from one to three of ten expert keywords per code. Four experts score 0–3; retain phrases scored 3 by at least two experts.
methods: Multilingual BERT classification, curriculum learning and expert-keyword reinforcement
method_details: Softmax ranks 284 product codes after staged manual/KSIC, TCB, enterprise, synthetic-keyword and expert-reinforcement training.
architecture: Firm-description encoder → product-code classification head → ranked code review by finance experts.
training: Fourfold stratified cross-validation, four epochs per fold/16 checkpoints; 90/10 train/validation also stated, without a clear reconciliation. Exact pretrained checkpoint/optimizer settings not established.
metrics: Label top-1 accuracy 45.8%; top-3 match 64.0%; top-5 match 70.1%. Expert agreement by rank: first 93.5%, second 83.2%, third 44.9% (not cumulative top-k accuracy).
baselines: No-curriculum and curriculum-only ablations versus full keyword-reinforced model; no broad competitive model benchmark.
evaluation_protocol: Stratified training/CV plus temporally new firm holdout; blind expert assessment of 785 firms. Full quantitative test size and relation between split schemes incompletely specified.
temporal_method: Temporally newer holdout; no explicit temporal representation or adaptive preference learner.
temporal_aspects: Updates firm/product taxonomy applicability; no sequential investor behavior.
explanation_method: Expert review of ranked product-code suggestions and confidence; no separate explanation generation or faithfulness test.
transparency: Semantic validity assessed by human experts; agreement should not be coded as trust, investment suitability or faithful model explanation.
implementation: Curriculum, model overview, ablations and expert assessment documented. Prototype integration is discussed; production deployment is not demonstrated.
open_science: Code/dataset release not reported in the paper.
